comments.content: But the last update was last week. Perhaps it would be in everybody's best interest if you only were assigned and focused on one task at a time?

Hey we should discuss this before you close and claim it. I expected this to be a huge project to make it run on the netlify backend for production, but then to only run on GitHub Actions for the bounty hunter forks. Can you verify that is the status?
As of now it looks you just reverted old code more-or-less, which I expect to not match the spec because it wasn't designed for that.

We should enable support from running the bot natively off of GitHub Actions again, but this time using `npx tsx index.ts` in order to eliminate the complexities around compilation, and then updating the `dist/index.js` file.
The bot should use GitHub Actions as the runtime environment for forks automatically for testing purposes. 
For production we should continue using a server less backend (we are currently using Netlify) this is because, from what I understand, the only way to easily add the bot from the GitHub Marketplace and immediately start using is if it is using an external backend. Otherwise, keeping all of the infrastructure on GitHub is preferred.

This is all unnecessary because we can run the bot using `npx tsx` so there's no need to commit the `dist/index.js` file anymore. This is in the spec https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/issues/310 @0xcodercrane 
Alternatively, we could consider building and uploading to some type of GitHub Action artifact storage and reload it every time the bot runs.
